rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person physically receives items (such as parts or goods) that arrive in batches, and the next activity starts after that receipt: Model each physical receipt that a person performs as a bpmn:manualTask performed by that person, placed in the flow where the receipt happens. Do not model the receipt as an intermediate catch event, because the person performs the work of receiving the items, and an event would only represent an occurrence affecting the flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person physically receives items (such as parts or goods) that arrive in batches, and the next activity starts after that receipt

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says items ordered from an outside supplier come in several separate deliveries at uncertain times, and a later step starts only when the first delivery is in hand: Model the wait for the first delivery as an intermediate catch event placed after the ordering activities and before the step that uses the items. Label the event with the arrival of the first delivery, using the description's arrival wording. Do not label it with the ordering or reordering verb of the earlier activity, and do not model the wait as a task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says items ordered from an outside supplier come in several separate deliveries at uncertain times, and a later step starts only when the first delivery is in hand

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a party acts on the records or outputs of an earlier activity after they are stored or handed over, such as following up on them later: Model this follow-up as its own task, placed after the activity that produces the records and in the lane or pool of the party that performs it. Connect it in sequence from the producing or storing step so the follow-up is not dropped or merged into the earlier task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a person must determine and record values (such as quantity, price and time) returned by several external sources, and a subsequent choice depends on those values, while the sources themselves are queried by a separate step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person must contact or query several external parties and collect specific attributes (such as quantity, cost and delivery time) from them before a decision on the next step is taken: Model the collecting of those attributes as a bpmn:userTask performed by that person, with software support, not as a generic bpmn:task. Place it before the exclusive gateway that decides on the next step, and connect it to that gateway with a sequence flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person must contact or query several external parties and collect specific attributes (such as quantity, cost and delivery time) from them before a decision on the next step is taken

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that work starts when the first of several arriving items is received, while receiving the remaining items and other follow-up actions such as reordering continue concurrently: Model the receipt of the first item as its own task on a branch that leaves a parallel split together with the follow-up actions, each branch starting with one unconditional flow. Join the first-receipt branch with a gateway before the work that starts on that receipt. Do not replace the receipt with an event-only element, and do not drop the follow-up actions from the split.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that work starts when the first of several arriving items is received, while receiving the remaining items and other follow-up actions such as reordering continue concurrently

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a check of an available quantity or level against a limit, where the result selects between alternative actions (for example a level that is found to be at or under a threshold, leading to a different reorder action): Model the check as an exclusive gateway whose label is a yes/no question that names the tested condition, phrased with the description's own wording (for example 'Has the level dropped to the limit?'). Do not label the gateway with a noun phrase that only names the quantity being checked. Give each outgoing flow a condition that states one outcome of the check, and connect each outcome to its own alternative action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a check of an available quantity or level against a limit, where the result selects between alternative actions (for example a level that is found to be at or under a threshold, leading to a different reorder action)
